subject: Comparing models with anova when using MLR

messages.author: 6158c2622f0f055d
messages.subject: Comparing models with anova when using MLR
parts:
Hi,

I have a question regarding model comparison when using MLR instead of ML estimator. When I want to compare two nested models using anova, it is clear that the chi square test results used in the anova are the ones obtained using ML, not MLR. Is there a way to change the anova command to use MLR results or does the difference have to be calculated "by hand"? And if so, what is the formula to include the scaling factors in the equation?

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re: Comparing models with anova when using MLR
parts:
That is not correct. Read through this article: Satorra, A., & Bentler, P. M. (2001). A scaled difference chi-square test statistic for moment structure analysis. Psychometrics, 66(4), 507-514.
Lavaan does this perfectly correctly and if you calculate it manually with the formulas, you will get the result produced by lavaan. The scaled test is not based on the difference of the scaled chisquares, but on a scaling of the difference of the non-scaled chisquares.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Comparing models with anova when using MLR
parts:
lavaan NOTE:
    The “Chisq” column contains standard test statistics, not the robust test that should be reported per model. A robust difference test is a function of two standard (not robust) statistics.

If I understand that correctly, it still uses standard, not robust chi square results?

Incorrect.  Read carefully.  It is only the "Chisq" column that contains standard test statistics.  The note is meant to prevent users from reporting those values by mistakenly thinking they are the individual models' fit statistics.  The chi-squared difference statistic is robust, as indicated just above the note your are referring to, where it says: "Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test", as well as all the evidence "car...@web.de" has provided.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
